# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 60 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 60 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_060_page_001.jpg

---

## Council Notes

Chapter 60 brings the Similitude 5 interpretation to its theological climax. The final exchange (60:5) introduces Pauline incorruption language (1 Cor 15:53: "this perishable must put on imperishable"). Hermas applies this to the moral order: the flesh that has been clothed with the Holy Spirit will be made to serve the spirit rather than rebel against it.

The statement "the Son of God was not content to give the commandments alone but bore their sins" is one of Hermas's most explicit atonement statements — combining commandment-giving and sin-bearing.

EMET's "fragile and imperishable" is a mixed pair — EMET likely means "fragile and perishable." LOGOS correctly renders "fragile and perishable." SOPHIA follows LOGOS.

The instruction "when you have clothed yourself with the Holy Spirit, clothe yourself also with the flesh" is a reversal of the expected order — the Spirit is to be put on first, then the flesh. This is Hermas's practical pneumatology: the Spirit must precede the body in moral priority.

---

## Similitude 5, Part 6 — The Son's Extra Work; Flesh and Spirit

**60:1** "Lord," I said, "why did the slave do more than he was commanded? Why did he dig and clear the vineyard when he had only been told to fence it?" "Listen," he said. "The slave is the Son of God, and the additional work he did beyond the commandment is a type of what he chose to do beyond what was required."

**60:2** "For the Son of God was not content merely to give the commandments to the people, but he himself bore their sins. This therefore is the additional work that the Son of God performed: he bore the sins of the people and suffered on their behalf."

**60:3** "When therefore he took counsel with the first-created angels regarding what reward should be given the slave for the additional work he had done, this is the deliberation concerning the flesh of the Son of God. For this flesh served the Spirit well and purely, not being defiled in any way in its conduct upon the earth. Therefore the reward was given to it."

**60:4** "The Father therefore took counsel with the Son and with the holy angels so that this flesh — which had served the Spirit blamelessly — should have some resting place and not lose the reward of its service. For every flesh that is found pure and unspotted, in which the Holy Spirit has dwelt, shall receive a reward."

**60:5** "You now have the interpretation of this parable." "I have it, lord," I said. "Lord," I continued, "hear me for one more moment." "Speak," he said. "Lord," I said, "the flesh is fragile and perishable." "So it is," he said. "But this perishable nature cannot put on incorruption unless first the Holy Spirit is joined to it; for a person cannot put on incorruption unless clothed with it. Therefore when you have clothed yourself with the Holy Spirit, clothe yourself also with the flesh, and the flesh will be made subservient to the Spirit."

---

*SOPHIA represents the consensus rendering of EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA, with rulings recorded in the Disagreement Log.*
